title: Zeros and f(x)=k
task: Solve an equation f(x)=k numerically by reading the point where the graphs meet.

steps.text: Type the function once as f(x)= followed by its expression.
For an equation f(x)=k, type y=k on a second line, and for a zero use the x-intercept of f.
Select the curve, click the gray point of interest, and choose Export Point to Expression List to read its coordinates.

lines.shows: a horizontal line meeting f at one gray point

exam_habit.text: A value read off a trace rather than solving for it is the error readers record, so the solution comes from the point of interest.
A value obtained from a graphing calculator without the equation, function or definite integral that was entered loses the setup point, so the setup is written beside the result.

sources.anchor_quote: When you graph an expression or equation, you will notice points of interest in gray on your graph.
Click a point of interest and then Export Point to Expression List to add it to a new expression line.
gray dots will appear at intercepts, intersection points, maximums, and minimums
find the zeros of functions (solve equations numerically)
students are required to write the setup (e.g., the equation being solved, or the derivative or definite integral being evaluated)
